# Query one engine-captured spectrum through browser and headless SDKs

Parent #763. Astra xhigh requirements-first scope, 2026-09-13. Source inspection baseline: main `cf9a620af4efa53672bfcdf48fc4757b5386b1bf`, with #775 and #777 delivered. Implement after accepted #779, reusing its actual endpoint/lifetime changes. Do not revive paused #774 or make this contingent on a generic subscription service. Luna max implements; Astra medium verifies concrete bugs against this scope.

## Required outcome and deliberate first slice

Original #763 requires engine-rendered spectra at selected track post-input-builtins, selected track post-matrix, and designated final output; independent L/R; portable worker-owned FFT; honest sample windows and validity; bounded capture/delivery; generated discovery; and browser/headless SDK access. Continuous streams, smoothing, sharing, SAB/qualified fallback and joins remain parent requirements, but a usable explicit spectrum read can precede them.

**Deliver one bounded, unsmoothed 2048-sample capture/query at any of all three required tap kinds through the actual SDK.** All three use the same graph observer/copy path; do not split them into three issues. The query captures the next complete window from the real prepared graph and stops capture when that window is complete. It is neither a source-buffer spectrum nor a continuous spectrum subscription.

Expose a small start/read/cancel operation using existing host request IDs and SDK request/reply conventions. Browser can provide an awaitable `querySpectrum({ target, channels })`; headless must let callers arm, explicitly render, then read/pump without an implicit second render engine or a promise that blocks the required render calls. Routine public naming is the implementer's choice. Return owned engine-generated frequency/L/R arrays and normalized profile/target metadata. Keep the common capture result and Rust analyzer reusable by the later stream; add no independent transport service.

## Minimal implementation and actual seams

1. **Prepare explicitly selected graph taps.** Extend `crates/host-core/src/prepare.rs`'s existing preparation path with optional spectrum target selection and checked capture resources (`spectrumLimits`, not generic public SDK `limits`). At its existing `GraphRuntimeBindings { observers: Vec::new(), ... }`, bind a small capture observer to `GraphNodeId::TrackStage` with `TrackStage::{PostInputBuiltins,PostMatrix}`, or the actual designated `GraphNodeId::Output`. Resolve IDs against the accepted compiled graph, using existing `graph-compiler/src/ids.rs` authorities. Selected target count/bytes are configurable resources, never a compiled track ceiling. Default/zero capacity binds no capture observers or PCM storage. Unprepared/unknown targets are typed refusals. Changing the prepared set uses the existing host reload/replacement boundary; no new live graph mutation API.
2. **Use the existing observation hook.** `graph/src/lib.rs::GraphRuntimeObserver` already receives `GraphObservationBlock { left, right, first_sample }`; `graph/src/runtime.rs::observe` already handles graph aliases and resident-bank lanes. A single implementation copies only selected channels into prepared storage while armed. Preserve actual boundary semantics in banked/aliased graphs; use `observe_resident` where needed to read a resident lane correctly. Do not add a new per-effect DSP kernel, source observer, or graph execution pass.
3. **Keep ownership small and bounded.** One outstanding capture/query per SDK engine path is enough. Prepare the capture window and ownership slots off render; use existing `engine::realtime::spsc::{bounded_spsc_move,bounded_spsc}` ownership where a queue is needed, with preallocated buffer return/credit handling. No new unsafe ring framework. Completed windows are immutable until the consumer releases them; render cannot overwrite or free reader-owned storage. Busy/capacity refusal is atomic. Completion, cancellation and worker failure leave no unbounded pending work, and capture is inactive between queries. Account capture storage separately from FFT scratch and transfer staging. Reuse fixed slots; no storage growth with session duration.
4. **Reuse host and analysis boundaries.** Add only bounded capture start/read/cancel plumbing in `hosts/host-web/src/{lib,ffi}.rs` and the shipped Worklet/host JS adapter. A Worklet message handler may copy a completed window; it must not run FFT/window/log math. `process()` performs only the Rust prepared capture copies and existing render operations: no new allocations, wrappers, postMessage sites, atomics notifications, waits or Worker wakes. Off-render SDK polling has at most one request in flight, a bounded rate, and a deadline/cancellation. Extend `sdk/src/browser/{response,response-worker}.ts` and `sdk/src/core/response.ts`'s existing analysis-only module protocol with spectrum evaluation; headless calls the same Rust analyzer between renders. A completed finite window transfers through the existing request/reply ownership path. This is not the continuous pooled fallback qualification and makes no zero-copy claim.
5. **Small common Rust analyzer.** Add `crates/host-core/src/spectrum.rs`, exported from its existing library, alongside `response.rs`. Accept immutable captured samples plus the engine profile; write axes and amplitudes into caller-provided output buffers. Use `microfft` 0.6.0's real `rfft_2048` with only the needed size features, through the normal workspace dependency/lockfile convention. Its documented in-place, no-allocation real FFT avoids a new FFT algorithm or planner framework. All analysis remains off render. Existing `math` supplies portable transcendental operations. `crates/dsp-reference/src/spectrum.rs::direct_dft_bin` is an independent small-fixture oracle, not the production algorithm. [microfft documentation](https://docs.rs/microfft/latest/microfft/)
6. **Generate discoverable facts.** Add one Rust-owned spectrum profile/tap descriptor consumed by existing `tools/parameter-metadata/src/{lib,abi_layout}.rs` generation and the SDK generated catalog. Report the three supported kinds, configured target availability, L/R selection, fixed window/FFT size, bin count, units/reference/floor, explicit-query cadence, no smoothing, and effective resource limits. Unsupported effect taps, FFT sizes and modes refuse explicitly. Update existing generated ABI assets/types and small browser/headless examples; no parallel hand-maintained JS capability list.

## Frozen signal, numerical and lifecycle semantics

- The fixed profile is `N=2048`, periodic Hann `w[n]=0.5-0.5*cos(2*pi*n/N)` for `0 <= n < N`. Prepare weights once off render; normalize by the sum of the actual stored weights. This is a declared implementation choice within the parent's Hann requirement. One-shot mode has no hop or smoothing history: advertise those as not applicable/none, not a fictional 30 Hz live rate. [Smith, spectrum analysis windows](https://www.dsprelated.com/freebooks/sasp/spectrum_analysis_windows.html)
- Output `N/2+1=1025` bins with `f[k]=k*sampleRate/N`. The real FFT is unnormalized. Interior amplitude is `2*abs(X[k])/sum(w)`; DC and Nyquist omit the factor two. Extract microfft's Nyquist value from the packed imaginary component of its DC entry; do not include it in DC's complex magnitude or discard it. Convert amplitude to `20*log10(A)` with a finite -120 dBFS lower floor, no upper 0 dB clamp. Full-scale bin-centered sine calibrates to 0 dBFS; this is amplitude, not broadband RMS or power density. Accumulate normalization/magnitude in f64 where appropriate; document denormal underflow to the finite floor. [microfft real-transform layout](https://docs.rs/microfft/latest/microfft/real/index.html)
- Validate sizes, selected channels, four launch sample rates, checked byte arithmetic and all finite captured samples before publishing any arrays. Nonfinite input invalidates the whole window with a typed status; do not sanitize audible PCM. Guard numerical overflow as a failure rather than publishing NaN/Infinity. No client-side FFT, window, spectral normalization or frequency-axis reconstruction.
- Start at the actual first observed engine block after successful arming. Copy exactly 2048 contiguous frames, including a partial final block if necessary; freeze the half-open `[startSample,endSample)` from the observer's u64 clock. Pending means fewer than 2048 frames have been captured. Missing/discontinuous blocks, successful source seek during a partial window, failed render, host replacement/reload/recreation or close invalidate pending capture; never concatenate across them. Cancellation is idempotent. A timeout/closed Worker releases or cancels its capture; no late result becomes a later query's result.
- Preserve known underrun information. `source/src/lib.rs::SourceConsumer::begin_block` already returns `SourceReadReport`, including underrun frames and active generation; `SourceGraphSourceSetDriver::begin_block` currently discards that report. Retain only the small validity information needed for capture and forward it through the existing graph observation boundary. A conservative flag meaning “a source underrun occurred in this graph during these captured blocks” is acceptable if explicitly labeled graph-wide; do not claim exact target/source attribution without it. Actual underrun zeros remain captured samples. Do not use the after-disarm cumulative telemetry as a fabricated exact live interval. Known seeks conservatively invalidate a partial capture even if target dependency is uncertain.
- Reuse the accepted #777/#779 current-host association and actual plan identity where exposed. Samples/tokens cross JS as bigint and JSON as declared decimal strings. Do not invent a global clock ID, effective curve revision or source/device timestamp. This is a measured signal window that may contain parameter changes; never label it with only the final response state as though that state generated the entire window. Capture time is not adjusted by DSP/PDC latency; keep any known latency metadata separate and do not invent mixed-route source-time mappings.
- Capture/analysis changes no audible samples, latency or tail. No request means no capture copies, FFT or analysis messages; capable prepared observers only perform their bounded inactive check. Native callers retain exclusive plan ownership and pump completed captures off render; no native thread wake is introduced.

## Few discriminating gates and delivery boundary

- **FFT calibration:** silence, DC, Nyquist alternating samples, bin-centered and off-bin sinusoids, impulse and distinct L/R. Compare selected bins against the existing f64 DFT oracle on the exact windowed samples; freeze a reasonable f32 FFT tolerance before running (e.g. normalized amplitude absolute error <=2e-5 for bounded unit-amplitude fixtures, calibration peaks within 0.01 dB). Verify floor, bin axis, invalid/nonfinite input and four launch rates. No extra corpus or listening gate for bit-identical observation.
- **Actual graph capture:** one prepared session with audibly different input-builtins/matrix/final-output signals proves all three tap identities and real rendered samples, including representative bank/tail/alias paths. Capture-on/off output is bit-identical. Verify exact N/span across a non-dividing render quantum, pending/cancel, a partial-window seek/gap, underrun validity, command changes within a window and a timestamp above 2^53.
- **Real SDK/lifetime/bounds:** actual headless explicit render/pump and shipped Chromium/Firefox/WebKit Worker queries return matching owned arrays. Exercise busy/unprepared/capacity refusal, delayed/dead Worker, timeout/close and same-position host replacement; results cannot be misattributed or overwrite held arrays. Zero capacity retains no capture lanes and idle has no copy/FFT/traffic. Existing allocation/callgraph/worklet resource/generated/ABI/package gates must cover the new path. A native/Wasm compile alone does not prove the browser endpoint.

Keep compiling local checkpoints, then one coherent usable endpoint candidate and existing official artifact/package/real-browser qualification boundary. No descriptive timing or optimization in this feature issue; use existing fail-closed discovery/report checks, no new harness. Astra medium blocks only actionable correctness/realtime/contract bugs and false claims against these frozen requirements; optional improvements belong in follow-ups.

## Parent work still required after this slice

Keep #763 open: common selective subscribe/update/poll/close, identical-job sharing and last-consumer disarm; change-driven response suppression; full engine/plan/state/content/publication/loss envelopes and parameter-change association inside windows; continuous block-aligned spectrum hop/rate, power smoothing and reset/warm-up epochs; shared bounded capture with SAB plus qualified pooled transfer fallback and slow-consumer loss accounting; packed remote vector telemetry/compatibility; bounded sample-time join; integrated examples/source-spectrum migration/resource evidence and the one frozen descriptive transport comparison. None is moved outside the parent. Parent-allowed later items remain arbitrary per-effect taps, phase/group delay, frozen-response mode where target mode shipped, device-clock mapping and extended compatibility/optimization.

## Implementation evidence

Luna max first native tranche adds optional selected-channel2048-frame graph capture and a portable microfft analyzer in existing host-core. The existing observer binding now permits the designated output node; its invalid-node test retains a genuinely unsupported node. Three focused tests pass, including real capture/analyze at all three required boundaries (/tmp/issue781-native-capture.*, exit0); formatting passes (/tmp/issue781-native-fmt.*, exit0). Root restores the unrelated Cargo.lock ordering while retaining the declared microfft dependency. This is a compiling native checkpoint, not endpoint acceptance. Actual underrun/seek/failed-render invalidation, existing console/meter host integration, full resource/lifetime gates and browser/headless delivery remain required in this same issue.

Luna max native validity/correction tranche carries actual graph-wide source underrun and generation discontinuity into windows, invalidates failed renders, and supports existing console/meter preparation. Astra medium early review identified natural-log dB conversion, pre-round Hann normalization and missing observer/ID retained rows; these are corrected using log10, stored f32 weights and actual retained metadata. Six focused spectrum tests pass, including actual three taps, seek invalidation, underrun and console/meter coexistence (/tmp/issue781-validity-spectrum3.*). The existing observer suites pass50 builtins and70 graph tests (/tmp/issue781-observer-tests3.*); the newly valid output tap required the inherited invalid-observer fixture to use a genuinely unsupported node while retaining its external ownership assertions. Root confirms all4 CAPI exact-resource tests pass (/tmp/issue781-root-capi-resources.*) and native formatting passes (/tmp/issue781-native-validity-fmt.*). Original failures remain in earlier logs. Host/FFI/SDK wiring and full endpoint/realtime/numerical qualification remain pending; no final acceptance is claimed.

Luna max first host/FFI/ABI tranche compiles and passes all7 existing ABI-layout tests, generated SDK checks and ABI validator/self-tests. Root locked host check and ABI checks also pass (/tmp/issue781-root-bridge-check2.*, /tmp/issue781-bridge-abi*). The additive bridge carries capture start/read/cancel and worker analysis through generated layouts. SDK wiring remains uncommitted/incomplete. Root identified unconditional spectrum staging allocation at boot: default/zero-capacity hosts must not retain PCM/FFT storage, so the next bounded correction makes buffers/analyzer lazy and charges actual storage. That known requirement remains open, alongside failed-render invalidation fixes and complete SDK/artifact qualification. This is a compiling recovery checkpoint, not endpoint acceptance.
